did_you_know.text: The chapter places a good name and favor above great wealth, describing a good reputation as more valuable than silver and gold.
The verse distinguishes between the prudent person, who sees danger and avoids it, and the naive, who continue on their way and suffer the consequences.
The verse emphasizes the importance of education: a child should be guided according to his way, in the hope that the habits he develops will remain with him into old age.
The chapter describes the imbalance of economic power: the rich rule over the poor, and the borrower becomes dependent on the lender.
Generosity toward the poor is presented as a blessed virtue: a generous person shares his bread with the needy and is rewarded with blessing.
According to the verse, the Lord watches over knowledge and preserves it, while the words of the treacherous may turn against them and fail.
The second part of the chapter opens with a call to pay attention to the words of the wise and listen to them with the heart, rather than merely hearing them superficially.
The verses teach that words of wisdom should be kept within and arranged on the lips so that they can guide a person in speech.
The chapter warns against robbing the poor or oppressing the needy, adding that the Lord will take up their cause and defend their rights.
The verse commands people not to move an ancient boundary stone—in other words, not to shift the boundaries established in the past by their ancestors.
